component.name: POPOPX
component.summary: Private and secure open-source messenger - no user IDs (not even random numbers)

description.p: Security assessment was done by Trail of Bits in November 2022.

ul.li: end-to-end encrypted messages, with editing, replies and deletion of messages.
sending end-to-end encrypted images and files.
secret chat groups - only group members know it exists and who is the member.
end-to-end encrypted audio and video calls.
portable chat profile - you can transfer your chat contacts and history to another device (terminal or mobile).
encrypted app database and files in the app storage (except videos).

Full privacy of your identity, profile, contacts and metadata: unlike any other existing messaging platform, POPOPX uses no phone numbers or any other identifiers assigned to the users - not even random numbers. This protects the privacy of who you are communicating with, hiding it from the relays that route your messages and from any observers.
Complete protection against spam and abuse: as you have no identifier on POPOPX platform, you cannot be contacted unless you share a one-time invitation link or an optional temporary user address.
Full ownership, control and security of your data: POPOPX stores all user data on client devices, the messages are only held temporarily on the relays until they are received.

Decentralized network: you can use POPOPX with your own servers and still communicate with people using the servers that are pre-configured in the apps or any other servers running the SimpleX Messaging Protocol.

description.p: You can connect to anybody you know via link or scan QR code (in the video call or in person) and start sending messages instantly - no emails, phone numbers or passwords needed.
Your profile and contacts are only stored in the app on your device - the relays your app talks to never see them, and POPOPX operates no relays of its own.
All messages are end-to-end encrypted using open-source double-ratchet protocol; the messages are routed via the relays your app is configured to use, over the open-source SimpleX Messaging Protocol.
Ask about this build in this fork's issue tracker: https://github.com/popopx-chat/popopx-chat/issues
The in-app option to connect to the developers opens a contact on a relay SimpleX Chat Ltd operates - upstream's team, not this fork's maintainers. The group directory is theirs too.
- the first release of the desktop app!
- message delivery receipts in small groups
- 6 new interface languages: Arabic, Bulgarian, Finnish, Hebrew, Thai and Ukrainian
